newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade says OSCE misunderstood elections.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade says OSCE misunderstood elections.

text.p: Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic said on Friday an OSCE delegation had delivered a "balanced" report on disputed local elections, but had confused some facts when it visited Belgrade last weekend.

Milutinovic made his remarks in response to a report by a delegation from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe which backed opposition claims that the authorities cheated it out of victories in polling on November 17.

Milutinovic told the official Tanjug news agency that the most important feature of the report was that it called for dialogue "within the framework of the system" and "discussion between the authorities and the opposition in parliament."

"I think it was a fairly good, constructive and balanced report," he said. "We accept the suggestions as well intentioned and constructive because they urged that everything should be considered within the institutions of our system."

Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, who led last weekend's OSCE mission to Belgrade, earlier urged President Slobodan Milosevic to install "real democracy" and respect opposition victories in the recent elections.
The mission came to Belgrade at Milosevic's invitation after the allegations of electoral fraud sparked weeks of opposition protests in the Serbian capital.
